detail: Native central 32x32 LDEC window; no interpolation. Geographic frame identification follows NASA documentation; no lat/lon conversion verified.

checks_completed: Exact source size and supplied SHA-256 match
Rasterio metadata, area registration, 5 m affine transform and polar stereographic CRS inspected
Only native window rows/columns 1584..1615 read; values and masks kept distinct
Counts checked finite, nonnegative and integral per returned valid pixel
Cell centers round-trip through source affine mapping

coordinate_system.frame: MOON_ME / DE421 (NASA README; not encoded by name in TIFF)
coordinate_system.reference_surface: Sphere radius 1737400 m (TIFF CRS); datum label unknown
coordinate_system.pixel_registration: Pixel area bounds from GeoTIFF; centers at column+0.5,row+0.5, consistent with NASA GMT pixel registration

summary.percentage_definition: 100 * observed_pixel_count / valid_pixel_count within returned bounds; null when denominator is zero or semantics are unverified.
summary.observation_rule: NASA defines LDEC as number of LOLA returns per pixel: positive integral count = observed; zero = unobserved; masked/NaN = nodata; other invalid values = unverified.

limitations: Observation counts only; not elevation, landing risk, suitability, safety or a recommendation.
Only central 160 x 160 m window; counts and percentage do not describe the entire 16 x 16 km source footprint.
TIFF datum is labelled unknown. MOON_ME/DE421 association is from official NASA product README; no independent absolute registration validation.
CRS/affine mapping verified in source X/Y metres only. No latitude/longitude conversion verified; render in source frame or withhold geographic globe overlay.
GeoTIFF nodata is NaN; schema forbids nonfinite numbers, so nodata_value is null and mask-defined status plus per-cell nodata preserve semantics.
Band unit tag is absent; returns-per-pixel interpretation comes from NASA LDEC documentation. Scale 1 and offset 0 are unchanged.
No interpolation, aggregation, gap filling or inferred values. Positive-count rule is count semantics, not a suitability threshold.
Source checksum matches the supplied local pin, not an independently published NASA checksum.
